items.name: Barrington Town Beach
items.blurb: Barrington's long sandy town beach faces Narragansett Bay. Seasonal swimming facilities serve both residents and visitors under the town's parking rules. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, parking, bike racks, dogs prohibited on managed beach sand during season.
items.hours: 2026 season May 23-September 7; lifeguards 9am-5pm and facilities until 7pm. Late-season service reduced to weekends because of staffing. · 2026 parking: resident day $6; nonresident $16 weekdays or $22 weekends/holidays. Resident season $40; qualifying resident seniors no charge. Walkers and bicyclists: no charge.

items.name: Nayatt / Daunis Road beach
items.blurb: A public path follows Mussachuck Creek toward a cobble beach on Narragansett Bay. The small access has very limited space for cars. Has: cobble beach, limited parking, no street parking.

items.name: Nayatt Point Beach
items.blurb: Nayatt Point Beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Rumstick Point barrier beach

items.name: Teed Avenue beach (Hundred Acre Cove)

items.address: Eastern end of Annawamscutt Drive, Bristol

items.name: Beach Road cobble beach (Bristol)
items.blurb: Steps below a roadside overlook reach a narrow cobble beach. High tide can cover the beach entirely. Has: tidal cobble beach, steps, limited street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Bristol Narrows beach and fishing area
items.blurb: A sandy peninsula and adjoining cobble shore lie near the mouth of the Kickemuit River. Dangerous water conditions make this a fishing access rather than a swimming beach. Has: sand and cobble shore, swimming prohibited, parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Camp St. Dorothy beach
items.blurb: State monitoring records identify a saltwater beach at Camp Saint Dorothy in Bristol. Current camp access and beach operations have not been confirmed. Has: camp beach.

items.name: Constitution Street beach
items.blurb: Stone steps through the seawall reach a small beach at the end of Constitution Street. The access is close to central Bristol Harbor and nearby timed street parking. Has: small beach, steps, nearby timed street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the end of Constitution Street, Bristol

items.name: Fales Road cobble beach
items.blurb: A concrete ramp at the end of Fales Road reaches the cobble shore of Narragansett Bay. The access is suitable for hand-carried boats rather than trailered launching. Has: cobble beach, ramp, limited street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Halsey Chase Herreshoff Park beach

items.address: At the intersection of Hope Street and Walley Street, Bristol

items.name: Independence Park beach
items.blurb: A small beach adjoins the launching area at Independence Park on Bristol Harbor. The park connects waterfront paths with the southern end of the East Bay Bicycle Path. Has: small harbor beach, parking, nearby restrooms, boat ramp, picnic tables, accessible park paths.

items.name: King Philip Avenue beach

items.address: Directly across from 25 King Philip Avenue, Bristol

items.name: Low Lane cobble beach

items.name: Mount Hope Fishing Access beach
items.blurb: A cobble beach and fringing marsh adjoin the state boat ramp. Swimming is prohibited at this fishing and boating access. Has: cobble beach, swimming prohibited, parking, boat ramp, no restrooms.

items.blurb: A public road beside the Mount Hope Bridge ends at a cobble beach. The shoreline provides views across Mount Hope Bay and space for hand-carried boat launching. Has: cobble beach, limited timed street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Sunrise Drive rocky beach

items.name: Surf Drive beach
items.blurb: A marked town right-of-way reaches a small rocky beach near the Warren River mouth. The shoreline has views of Rumstick Point and Narragansett Bay. Has: rocky beach, limited street parking.

items.blurb: Ocean beach and saltwater-fishing access beside the breachway.

View it from a boat or from the breakwater across the harbor at Sauga Point without entering the private property. Has: standing former lighthouse, private residence, no public entry, best shore viewing spot: Sauga Point breakwater across Wickford Harbor, best close view: boat, boat tour: Rhode Island Bay Cruises https://www.fastferry.com/rhode-island-bay-cruises/, viewing reference: https://www.newenglandlighthouses.net/poplar-point-light-history.html.
items.address: Poplar Point at the southern entrance to Wickford Harbor, North Kingstown, RI

items.name: Rhode Island Bay Cruises — Lighthouse and Newport Harbor Tour
items.blurb: This narrated cruise from Quonset covers the lower bay and Newport Harbor. Its ten advertised lighthouse stops include the remains of Whale Rock, and the trip provides water views without lighthouse landings. Has: boat tour, narrated cruise, passes Poplar Point, passes Plum Beach, passes Dutch Island, passes Whale Rock ruins, passes Beavertail.
items.address: 1347 Roger Williams Way, North Kingstown, RI
items.hours: 2026 season ended; return announced for 2027; published 2026 departures at 1 pm or 2 pm on designated dates; duration 100 minutes · 2026 advance fares: adults 12-59 $45; seniors 60+ $43; children 3-11 $30; infants 0-2 no charge with reservation; walk-up fares $5 higher

items.name: Hog Island Shoal Lighthouse
items.blurb: This offshore iron lighthouse stands near the entrance to Mount Hope Bay. A boat provides the best view, with a more distant shore view from the old ferry landing in Portsmouth. Has: standing lighthouse, privately owned, no public landing or tower tours, best shore viewing spot: old ferry wharf at the end of Bristol Ferry Road in Portsmouth, binoculars useful, boat tour: Save The Bay https://savebay.org/family-fun/lighthouse-tours/, passing ferry: https://prudencebayislandstransport.com/.
items.address: Hog Island Shoal, southeast of Hog Island, Narragansett Bay, RI, Portsmouth

items.name: Prudence Island Lighthouse (Sandy Point Light)
items.blurb: Prudence Island's granite lighthouse retains its distinctive birdcage lantern. Reach the island by ferry and walk south from the landing to Sandy Point for close exterior views; the tower is closed. Has: standing lighthouse, grounds viewing, no tower entry, best viewing spot: Sandy Point at end of Landing Lane, approximately one-mile walk from ferry landing, ferry: https://prudencebayislandstransport.com/, passing boat tour: Save The Bay https://savebay.org/family-fun/lighthouse-tours/.
items.address: Landing Lane at Sandy Point, Prudence Island, Portsmouth, RI

items.name: Save The Bay — Ultimate Lighthouse Tour
items.blurb: This seven-hour narrated trip travels from Providence through both main passages of Narragansett Bay. It covers active and former lighthouse stations and stops at Rose Island for lunch and time on the grounds. Has: boat tour, narrated cruise, Rose Island landing, lunch, binoculars supplied, route includes Beavertail, Bristol Ferry.
items.address: 100 Save The Bay Drive, Providence, RI 02905
items.hours: Selected dates June/September/October 2026, 9 am-4 pm; published 2026 season ended; future dates not posted · Adults $150; members/seniors/children 3-12 $140; children under 3 no charge; lunch included

items.name: Latimer Reef Lighthouse (New York; visible from Rhode Island)
items.blurb: Latimer Reef's offshore lighthouse stands in New York waters but can be seen from Napatree Point in Westerly. It is privately owned and closed to visitors, with closer views available on Cross Sound's Lights & Sights cruise. Has: standing lighthouse outside Rhode Island, best Rhode Island shore viewing spot: Napatree Point Conservation Area in Westerly, distant view, binoculars useful, no public landing or tower tour, boat tour: Cross Sound Lights & Sights https://www.lighthouse.cruises/, eyewitness shore-view reference: https://trailsandwalksri.wordpress.com/tag/history/page/9/.
items.address: Latimer Reef, Fishers Island Sound, New York, Southold, New York

items.name: Conimicut Lighthouse

Has: standing lighthouse, no public entry, best shore viewing spot: Conimicut Point Park, boat tour: Save The Bay https://savebay.org/family-fun/lighthouse-tours/, charter route: https://www.biggamefishingri.com/lighthouse.php, checked 2026-11-01.

items.name: Warwick Neck Lighthouse (Warwick Light)
items.blurb: Warwick Neck's lighthouse stands at the southern end of the peninsula. A boat offers the best view, with only a limited land view from the gate at the end of Warwick Neck Avenue. Has: standing lighthouse, no regular public station or tower entry, best viewing spot: boat off Warwick Neck, limited shore view: gate at end of Warwick Neck Avenue, boat tour: Save The Bay https://savebay.org/family-fun/lighthouse-tours/, viewing reference: https://www.newenglandlighthouses.net/warwick-lighthouse.html, checked 2026-11-01.

items.name: Watch Hill Lighthouse

items.hours: Grounds daily 8 am-sunset year-round; museum July-August: Tuesday-Friday noon-4 pm with Thursday until 8 pm and Saturday 4-8 pm; tower and keeper's residence closed · Donations welcome
